observations: Mātha as road is a literal terminal member for this rule and is named with separate padavī and anupada exceptions.
Bāla and Tattva explain the lexical path and Tattva gives object-sense ghañ. The Dhātupāṭha fixes the root as mathe viloḍane. The straight path uses rod shape.
The Kāśikā toll word contains long ā, while Nyāsa's output in this display has short a even though the gloss gives the long base.
Nyāsa restricts anupada to following closely and identifies other anu compounds as outside the selected source relation.
The same ā+krand family supplies two admitted locale readings: cries are heard there or distressed people go there for refuge.
Both teaching suffixes are explicitly allowed and Vasu prints the initial/final accent pair.
Kit taddhita targets the last pitch position. The ñ-it suffix targets the initial position.
Kāśikā prints ākrandikī and 4.1.15 expressly lists both relevant affixes for feminine ṅīp.
The actual pada member is lexical in the word-taker input. A bahuc prefix supplies no qualifying former compound member.
Nyāsa’s kecit extends the predicate to ślokapādapadam as an identified construction.
The tail of the online 4.4.37 Tattva paragraph discusses padottarapada, aligning topically with 4.4.39. The exact print lineage of the display remains Open.
Nyāsa and Tattva identify both distributed-throat and facing-throat meanings, and reject the prādi ‘has reached the throat’ compound.
Artha and lalāma are independent lexical inputs. Bāla glosses the latter as a mark.
Bhaṭṭi uses a separate anupadī pursuit descriptor. This does not create another input or equivalent taddhita suffix under 4.4.37.
